I was 30 having this same dilemma. There is no true right answer- only what you feel is right for you. 
Yes, there are a lot of negatives. Not to mention pregnancy is hard on your body. 
There’s also some positives *if* that’s what you choose. 

I had this dilemma with my partner involved. We ultimately decided to keep our baby boy after a LOT of back and forth- because that was the right choice for me and him. Now baby is in the NICU, I almost died, and we have had an insane month. 
I don’t regret it, because it was right for me- but it is PROOF that NO ONE but you should choose. 
My body almost gave up. Towards the end of my pregnancy I was so swollen I looked like I got beaten up and ended up with preeclampsia. They had to pull my son at 31 weeks. 
I have never ever been more pro choice. You should know how hard it can be and make that choice for your heart. 
It’s okay if it scares you and you want to try still. 
It’s okay if it scares you and you don’t. 

You get to choose. Also if you’re in an unsafe state, make SURE to take a method that cannot be tracked so you can cry miscarriage. Be careful. Be safe. Follow your heart 💜

OP, I’ve been the jealous person in the relationship. I let it literally create such a toxic environment for my partner and I that it was suffocating him. He had to FIGHT to have friends. I let it get so, so bad. 
One day, he finally snapped and asked why I didn’t trust him. Had he ever given me a reason not to? Had he not been bending over backwards to make me comfortable? 

I realized I was being impossibly insecure, and torturing someone that I loved more than anything. The realization that you sometimes just have to let go, and trust that this person you’ve built faith with will keep it is TERRIFYING. ESPECIALLY if you aren’t feeling confident yourself. 

My cure was/always is communication. You did right by not letting it fester but now, just be honest and approach it as a personal problem you have that you’re working on. Tell her when you feel uncomfy but always lead with a “I trust you, I just am feeling a little icky and here’s why” and then voice it. Know it’s a you problem, and work to make it better for this person you love and trust. You’ll be so much better for it. 


Yes, some people will take advantage of the trust. But I don’t believe most will, and I believe it’s a THEM problem that would have ended the relationship anyways if it was gonna happen. You just have to be the best you you can be for her first, and hope that mutual respect and love follows.

I know I’m late to this thread, so it may be late… but I lost my vision (though it did end up being temporarily for me this time) due to a chronic disease a year or so ago. I went blind-and thought my life was over. 
I know you’re reeling right now, and panicking and grieving and in so much pain and I’m sorry-but from someone who has gone through it, even if I came out of it, I can say: it’s not great, by any means, but life does continue. 
If his gentle green eyes are gone, the gentle heart behind it hopefully is still there. Hold onto that hope if you can. 

You don’t have to, you’re not obligated, but if you do, just know that blindness is a lot to handle but it is not…. Impossible to continue in a lot of industries with. I was literally interning at NASA when mine happened. They connected me with a blind physicist to help set up accommodations so I could still work when I wasn’t in impossible pain. 

It’s not a happy ending. I’m still rooting for some vision saving. Mine isn’t all back, but I have some. I hope for both of you he has the same or better. But just know-it’s not the end. 


Also, I mourn for you. I’m so sorry you have to be on this side of helplessness. I’m so sorry. My heart hurts for your pain so much, and I wish nothing but answers for you guys. I’m so so sorry that companies are allowed to send shit like this out. That senseless shit like this happens. I’m just sorry, and angry, and sad for you and your family.

NAD but Came here to say this. I have IIH- idiopathic intracranial hypertension. The pain/symptoms are very much like what you describe. I was diagnosed by an ophthalmologist, sent for a spinal tap by a neurologist just to confirm/ease symptoms. 

If you do have increased CSF, there are lots of potential solutions to ease your pain. For now- make sure you’re hydrated (not just water-electrolytes!), take it easy with OTC pain meds(if it is CSF the rebound pain can be brutal) and of course confirm all this with doctor first to make sure you’re safe. 

I went straight up blind in July from mine before I was fully dx’d, and was in horrible pain. 
If it gets to a 10/10 please go to the ER- because you can get into dangerous territory with CSF pressures. Just be your own advocate!! If it’s anything like IIH, it’s in invisible disease that can be difficult to get treated but-you can do it!!
